observationsNotFindings: The split is the tightest delta I have seen in this sweep. One grouped obligation becomes three, one per ACTIVE fixture class, and all six carried obligations are byte-identical objects rather than rewrites. That makes the whole change auditable in a single diff, and it is why the FC-APPLIC flip can be assessed on its own without re-checking the rest of the row.

This join uses findingDisposition to record its own delta, FC-APPLIC-TABLE-AUTHORED, with structured landedAt values pointing at both places the measurement lands. I noted the opposite pattern on the monorepo join, which recorded its landing only in a free-text lands array while leaving findingDisposition carrying older findings. This is the better of the two conventions and worth standardising on.

The evidence base under DR-122 is thin in a way no single artifact discloses. Four of the five cited verdicts have no Codex counterpart, and three of those four are dated today. Nothing here is misstated - every single-reviewer pin says 'Codex not reviewed' - but the row's accumulated design standing now rests substantially on one reviewer, and the coordinator is the only party positioned to see that across artifacts.

OBL-FC-APPLIC is bucketed under specifiedNotLeftover alongside OBL-PREVIEW-NOT-ADVERTISED and OBL-G17, which are specified inside v15 itself, whereas FC-APPLIC's table was authored in a separate artifact. The disposition is right and the reason says plainly where the table lives, but the bucket name flattens a real distinction between specified-in-contract and authored-elsewhere. Not charged; noted in case a later version wants a distinct bucket.
